saver.interpretation: QAIRT converter recognizes/canonicalizes only the baseline block4 activation expression into a single QNN GELU op. The mathematically equivalent block5-style diagnostic expression prevents that recognition and leaves the explicit activation chain.

canonical.first_relevant_failure: no properties registered for q::QNN_Gelu; could not create op q::QNN_Gelu; generated node _elementwiseneuron_0

decanonicalized.later_failure: could not create q::flat_from_vtcm from ReluMinMax; generated node _Clip

host_htp_context_probe.interpretation: The block4 expression change alters the HTP graph-finalize path: canonicalized graph reaches/fails at QNN_Gelu; decanonicalized graph eliminates that failure and advances to a later unrelated Clip/flat_from_vtcm limitation of the x86 host HTP route. This proves structural HTP-path sensitivity but does not prove target-device behavior.

conclusion: Host numerical localization, Saver replay, and RouterX86 HTP compile all converge on block4 activation pattern recognition/lowering as a real structural sensitivity. Next device-side structural evidence should test whether target HTP compilation also maps canonical block4 to a native/fused GELU path while the equivalent decanonicalized expression remains explicit/different.
